cpu_percent_denominator: One logical CPU core; sampled CPU tick deltas divided by sampled phase elapsed time.
aggregation: Median of three trial medians, with trial ranges and largest observed peak reported separately. PSS+SwapPss is summed per sample before statistics.

environment.data: Fresh empty launcher root per run

limitations: Sampled maxima are observed lower bounds, not a guarantee for all application states.
Processes born and exited wholly between /proc reads can be missed; sequential reads are not atomic.
RSS sums can count shared pages more than once; PSS and SwapPss remain separate raw measurements.
VmHWM is the kernel main-process lifetime RSS counter, not peak PSS or a process-tree counter; its accounting can differ from smaps_rollup.
Xvfb is measured before and during the app and reported separately; it remains real system cost.
The Python observer and X11 driver are test-process work, excluded from launcher and display totals.
CPU totals require stable sampled identities; common-process CPU during churn is only a lower bound.
This is a shared development host with no system-wide cache flush or CPU isolation.
Expose request frequency does not prove rendered FPS.
Empty-library activity does not cover file operations, login, downloads or Java/game memory.
The six runs are three adjacent baseline/candidate pairs on one shared Linux/Xvfb host; this is not randomized or confidence-interval analysis.
The configured 5 ms sampling sleep is added to sequential read overhead; observed drawing intervals are reported separately.
Optimized run 2 includes application and Xvfb swap; lower resident RSS or PSS alone cannot establish lower allocated memory.
Application source revisions differ only in documentation/site/packaging files according to git diff --stat; framework revisions and binaries differ.
CPU reduction applies to the complete empty-library window under this Expose workload, not FPS, interactive latency, file/login/download work, or Windows/macOS runtime performance.
Rectangle microbenchmark figures are not included or extrapolated to whole-window speedup.

audit.note: Complete sampled readouts do not rule out short-lived processes or memory/CPU events wholly between samples.

column_definitions.percent_change: Positive means candidate larger; negative means candidate smaller. Null when baseline is zero.
